markets.rules_secondary:
How this is resolved

The market solely resolves to the publication date visibly displayed on the "Presidential Actions" tab at whitehouse.gov at 10:00 AM ET the following day.

Payout criteria

The actions may include proclamations, executive orders, nominations & appointments, and memoranda.
Any item listed on the page counts, regardless of its legal effect.

Examples (for Jan 10, 2026):

Executive Order with a Jan 7 signing date is released with a Jan 10 publication date → resolves Yes
Proclamation e-mailed to White House Press Pool but not uploaded by 10:00 AM next day → resolves No
Proclamation is released Jan 10 with a backdated Jan 9 publication date → resolves No
Bill signed into law and shows up on "Briefings & Statements" instead of "Presidential Actions" → resolves No

markets.rules_primary: If Donald Trump signs an Executive Order on Nov 19, 2026 (as shown by its full text, published on whitehouse.gov or released to the White House press pool before 10:00 AM ET on Nov 20, 2026), then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
How this is resolved

A day counts only if the full text of an Executive Order that Donald Trump signed that day is published on whitehouse.gov or released to the White House press pool, as shown by a pool report that includes its full text, before 10:00 AM ET the following day. If neither happens, the market resolves to No.
Pool reports, statements, fact sheets and remarks saying that Donald Trump signed an Executive Order do NOT count without its full text, including when they come from the White House.
The signing date on the document governs, not the publication date.

Payout criteria

Only Executive Orders count. Memoranda, proclamations, determinations and orders that are not Executive Orders do NOT count, even if whitehouse.gov lists them under "Executive Orders".
For example, "Regarding the Proposed Acquisition of the United States Steel Corporation by Nippon Steel Corporation" (Jun 13, 2025) is listed under "Executive Orders" on whitehouse.gov but was published in the Federal Register as an order, not an Executive Order, so it does NOT count.
If it is unclear whether a document is an Executive Order, the Exchange may wait for its publication in the Federal Register, where only a numbered Executive Order counts.
